_comment: PROPOSED basal schedule (local clock, units U/hr). NOT applied to the live Nightscout profile. Evidence-based redesign calibrated to Loop's actual delivered basal (see REPORT.md section 11). Phased rollout recommended. Apply only via care-team / Loop workflow.

basal_step1._desc: Step 1 (applied to Loop 2026-06-13 06:48 UTC): overnight cut + midday trough + late-dinner taper.
basal_step1._night1_result: First night overshot to HIGHS overnight: mean 156, max 214, 17% >180, 0% lows. Rise tracked the 22:30 taper (118->157). Midday trough worked well (today 11:00-13:00 ran 83-119, no lows). Conclusion: evening taper too deep; deep-overnight cut was fine. See basal_step1b.

basal_step1b._desc: Step 1b (applied to Loop 2026-06-13 23:25 UTC): walk back evening/overnight cut, keep midday trough.
basal_step1b._week_result: 7-day result (Jun 14-20) vs 90d baseline. NOTE: Jun 17 was sensor day-1 (Dexcom started Jun 16 16:32) and read jumpy-low (29% lows, min 45) - excluded below. EXCL sensor day-1: OVERNIGHT 00-04 SOLVED (%<70 3.1, %<54 0.3, TIR 96.9 - better than goal). Evening fine (%<70 5.4, %<54 0.8) - the low creep was sensor noise, leave it. Dawn 04-07 lows REAL (%<70 9.7, not sensor) -> Step-1c cuts dawn. Midday 11-16 lows REAL (%<70 14.9) and rose despite basal cut => meal/bolus-driven, review lunch carb-ratio. Overall %<70 8.6 / %<54 0.4.

basal_step1c._desc: Step 1c (applied to Loop 2026-06-20 21:33 UTC): cut dawn 04:30 1.55->1.35.
basal_step1c._result: Reviewed Jul 4 (14d, incl. G6->G7 swap Jun 26; G7 warmup auto-excluded). G7 reads same level as G6 (mean 108 vs 110) so comparisons valid. Dawn FIXED (9.7->5.6% <70). Midday improved a lot (15->7.3%, real not calibration). Overnight up to 6.4% but all shallow (nadir 61-67, 0% <54) and partly G7 compression lows -> HOLD basal, don't chase. Severe lows 0.0-0.4% everywhere; excellent control. Verdict: Step-1c is a keeper; hold and watch overnight (behavioral/sensor-placement fix for compression, not basal).

basal_step2._desc: Step 2 (after ~1 week confirming step 1): trim the daytime shoulders (09:30 and merge 16:00-20:00). Merges the old 16:00/17:00 boundaries into one 1.45 afternoon block.

basal_step1d._desc: Step 1d (proposed, LOW PRIORITY - evidence weakened on review): 09:30 1.80 -> 1.45. See _evidence and _revision.
basal_step1d._evidence: 45d review (Jun 9-Jul 24), morning window. FINDING: there is effectively no breakfast - only 35% of days have a >=15g morning carb entry and median first food is 11:18am; the 4/6/8am small entries are corrections at BG~200, not meals. Early morning 04:00-09:00 is GOOD (median 108->118, modest +10 dawn rise, ~0-4% lows, ~0-3% highs) - do not touch. The problem is the LATE-MORNING FASTING SAG: on days with no food before 11:00, 14/16 drifted down, median -16 mg/dL (worst -40/-36/-69), 31% dipped <70, arriving at the first meal already low. Cause: the schedule jumps to 1.80 U/hr at 09:30 (highest daytime rate) mid-fast - apparently vestigial coverage for a breakfast no longer eaten. Loop fights it: hour 10 delivers 1.24 vs 1.80 scheduled, 25% suspended (hr 11: 0.81 vs 1.25, 29% suspended). Morning is the cleanest window for analysis (~0.2 Afrezza-like drops/wk, few fake carbs), so this is fasting-grade evidence.
basal_step1d._revision: REVISED after learning the subject is SLEEPING IN (summer). The 09:00-11:30 window is therefore still SLEEP, not a daytime fast, so the same G7 compression that inflates overnight lows also applies here (lying on the sensor). Re-running with compression episodes excluded: median fasting drift shrinks from -16 to -9 mg/dL (11/12 days still fall, so direction is robust but magnitude halved), and %<70 in 09:00-11:30 falls to ~0-4% (the '31% dipped <70' was largely artifact). The 'Loop is suspending 25%' signal is also partly circular - compression lows cause Loop to suspend. Landing at ~96-101 before the first meal is acceptable. VERDICT: the 09:30 bump is still anomalous but the case for changing it is weak and the pattern is SEASONAL (will shift when school resumes). Prefer to hold, or use a Loop Override on sleep-in days rather than editing the permanent schedule.

first_meal_review_2026_07_24._desc: First-meal-of-day analysis (the real 'breakfast', ~12:18 due to summer sleep-in). The best-supported meal-side finding to date, because the morning window is comparatively free of unlogged Afrezza (~0.2/wk) and fake carbs (>=25g filter).
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._finding: Strongly asymmetric: 22% of first meals dip <70 within 4h vs only 2% peaking >180, with median peak just 135. The dose is a touch strong for the starting point - he arrives at ~89 already drifting down, then boluses at an effective CR of 5.7 (stronger than the profile's 6).
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._option: Weaken the first-meal carb ratio in the window he actually eats (currently ~10:00-15:00): CR 6 -> 7. A 50g meal would take ~7.1U instead of ~8.3U (~1.2U less, ~60 mg/dL at ISF 53). Expected: most of the 22% lows resolve; peak rises from ~135 toward ~150-160, still well under 180. SEASONAL CAVEAT: the window is tied to the summer sleep-in and will need revisiting when the schedule shifts.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._caution: Single-variable discipline: do NOT combine with a basal change. ISF stays unvalidated (corrections are mostly invisible Afrezza/fake-carb).
